meta.title_alt1: why AI can't count the R's in strawberry

meta.spine: the model never reads your words. it reads the pieces.
meta.description: why can a supercomputer pass the bar exam but fail to count the letter R in strawberry? because it never sees letters — it sees numbered tiles called tokens, and those tiles quietly control your bill, your memory, and a hidden global language tax.

lines: User: How many R's in strawberry?
AI: There are 2 R's in strawberry.

beats.vo: The machine never reads your words. | Before the model sees a single sentence you type, a hidden blade chops your text into numbered puzzle tiles called tokens.
beats.say: The machine never reads your words. | Before the model sees a single sentence you type, a hidden blade chops your text into numbered puzzle tiles called tokens.

beats.vo: Every tile is a click on a running taximeter. | You pay for the tiles in your question, and you pay again for every tile in the machine's answer.
beats.say: Every tile is a click on a running taximeter. | You pay for the tiles in your question, and you pay again for every tile in the machine's answer.

beats.vo: Those tiles also share a single bucket called the context window. | Even a one-million-token bucket is just a working desk — and when the desk fills up, the oldest tiles quietly fall off the edge.
beats.say: Those tiles also share a single bucket called the context window. | Even a one-million-token bucket is just a working desk — and when the desk fills up, the oldest tiles quietly fall off the edge.

beats.vo: Here is the unfair part nobody advertises. | Because the chopper was trained mostly on English text, saying the exact same sentence in another language gets chopped into two or three times as many tiles.
beats.say: Here is the unfair part nobody advertises. | Because the chopper was trained mostly on English text, saying the exact same sentence in another language gets chopped into two or three times as many tiles.

beats.vo: Even a single emoji can shatter into several hidden tiles, while invisible system instructions eat your budget before you type a word. | Once you see the chopper, you know how to beat it: keep prompts lean, trim dead history, and remember that strawberry was always just two tiles.
